newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SOCCER-BELGIAN CLUB AALST CLEARED OF BRIBERY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BELGIAN CLUB AALST CLEARED OF BRIBERY.

text.p: Belgian first division club Aalst was cleared on Tuesday of allegations of attempted bribery to fix matches, the Belgian soccer union said.
The union's controlling committee ruled that both the club and its manager Patrick Orlans were innocent of the allegations.

However, former Aalst youth coach Eddy Roelandt and Bart De Bruyne, a players' agent who worked with the club in the past were found guilty of attempted bribery and given a two-year and 10-year suspension respectively.
"The control committee has acquitted...the accused Orlans and Aalst of the fact of which they had been accused," Jef Van Dijck, deputy chairman of the committee told the hearing.
"If you didn't do it you can't be punished," a relieved Orlans told reporters after the ruling.
Aalst were prominent relegation candidates in late March when they were 17th in the 18-team table, eight points behind 16th-placed Mechelen.
But they staged a remarkable comeback to finish the season two months later in 15th place, five points clear of Mechelen, who were relegated with Cercle Brugge.
Aalst won four of their last six league games and drew the two others. In the previous 28 rounds they had won just four matches and lost 14.
Aalst attributed the turnaround largely to a change of coach earlier this year.
Belgian soccer union prosecutor Rene Verstringhe had called for Aalst to be fined up to 1.75 million francs ($48,900) and for Orlans to be suspended for a year.
He also demanded a suspension for Roelandt, alleged by players from other clubs who gave evidence to the committee to have acted as an intermediary for Aalst.
Verstringhe had also demanded a 10-year suspension for De Bruyne, who was alleged to have acted as an intermediary. He is currently in Nigeria.
